skill.name: forensics-osquery
skill.description: Use osquery for authorized endpoint forensics, incident triage, and threat hunting across Linux, macOS, and Windows.
skill.summary: Build and apply read-only osquery investigations for endpoint evidence, suspicious activity, and continuous monitoring.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate defensive osquery guide, and most static hits are false positives from detection SQL, Markdown, loopback addresses, and sensitive-path indicators. Confirmed risks are endpoint telemetry collection, privileged install or service commands, and an unbundled relative script instruction. Additional concerns include ineffective credential-file detection, potential registry secret logging, and unverified privileged package bootstrapping.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the registry data column, narrow approved keys, and redact sensitive values before logs leave the endpoint.
Use supported file event or operating-system audit telemetry, then test the detector against controlled password-file reads.

remediation.issue: Privileged package bootstrap lacks independent verification
remediation.suggestion: Use a scoped signed-by keyring, verify the full key fingerprint or package checksum, and pin reviewed package versions.
Bundle reviewed scripts with integrity metadata or remove execution instructions and provide complete read-only commands instead.

remediation.issue: FleetDM example uses a fixed placeholder password
remediation.suggestion: Replace the value with a secret-manager reference and state that deployments must generate a unique credential.

remediation.issue: Scheduled endpoint telemetry can contain sensitive data
remediation.suggestion: Document authorization, least privilege, encryption, access control, retention, and redaction requirements beside every deployable pack.

semantic_findings.title: Unbundled Relative Script Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow instructs users to execute ./scripts/osquery_triage.sh, but the reported package contains no scripts directory. A same-named local file could be executed unintentionally.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command and script claims are explicit, while the code-filled file structure lists no scripts directory or script files.

semantic_findings.title: Ineffective Credential-File Access Detection
semantic_findings.description: The credential-file detector joins process_memory_map and treats mapped paths as file-access evidence. Password files are normally read, not memory-mapped, so the query can miss real access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: All three examples use process_memory_map as a proxy for file reads, which does not generally record ordinary reads of password files.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Registry Secret Logging
semantic_findings.description: A scheduled query selects registry data from keys containing Credentials or Password. With result logging enabled, plaintext credential-like values could enter osquery logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The query explicitly selects the data column every hour, and the bundled configuration enables filesystem result logging.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Privileged Package Bootstrap
semantic_findings.description: The deployment guide imports repository trust material and installs packages as root without a documented fingerprint, checksum, or pinned-version verification step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands fetch trust material over the network and immediately use privileged package tooling without an independent integrity check.

semantic_findings.title: Copyable Placeholder Database Password
semantic_findings.description: The FleetDM example includes a fixed fleet_password value without an adjacent instruction to replace it, increasing the chance of an insecure copied configuration.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The password is visibly a placeholder, but the example gives no local replacement or secret-management requirement.

content.value_statement: Endpoint investigations often require many platform-specific tools and commands. This skill provides osquery workflows, detection queries, and packs for consistent forensic collection across major platforms.
actual_capabilities: Creates read-only osquery queries for processes, users, files, network activity, persistence, and system configuration.
Maps threat-hunting queries to MITRE ATT&CK techniques.
Adapts investigation approaches for Linux, macOS, and Windows tables.
Provides bundled osquery packs for triage, persistence, lateral movement, and credential access monitoring.
Explains osqueryd deployment, scheduling, logging, fleet enrollment, and performance tuning.
Structures incident triage and evidence review workflows for authorized endpoints.
limitations: Requires osquery and relevant platform tables; some examples reference scripts that are not included.
Many queries require elevated access and can collect sensitive endpoint telemetry.
Does not acquire disk images, memory dumps, recover deleted files, or validate evidence independently.
Example queries require schema and performance testing because platform or version differences can cause errors or incomplete results.

use_cases.title: Triage a suspected endpoint
use_cases.description: Collect process, login, network, persistence, and recent file metadata using authorized read-only queries.

use_cases.title: Hunt a MITRE ATT&CK technique
use_cases.description: Select relevant endpoint artifacts, tailor detection queries, and document evidence for a defined hunting hypothesis.

use_cases.title: Build continuous osquery monitoring
use_cases.description: Design scheduled query packs with suitable intervals, logging controls, platform filters, and resource limits.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare basic endpoint triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized, read-only osquery triage plan for [platform]. Cover processes, users, network connections, persistence, and evidence handling.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate persistence
prompt_templates.prompt: Design read-only osquery checks for suspected persistence on [platform]. Explain each artifact, expected benign results, suspicious indicators, and required privileges.

prompt_templates.title: Hunt credential access
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an authorized osquery hunt for credential-access technique [MITRE ID]. Avoid collecting secret contents and include validation steps for every detection assumption.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production monitoring pack
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose an osqueryd monitoring pack for [environment]. Include platform constraints, intervals, expected volume, privacy controls, false-positive tuning, and staged validation.

output_examples.input: Triage a Linux server with unusual outbound connections.
output: Start with process-to-socket correlation and exclude only verified infrastructure addresses.
Review process ancestry, executable paths, command lines, users, and start times.
Preserve results with timestamps and document every environment-specific exclusion.

output_examples.output: Review enabled tasks, actions, paths, owners, and recent execution times. Prioritize user-writable locations and encoded command interpreters for validation.
Collect process and event metadata without secret values. Validate suspicious commands against approved administration activity and protect all exported telemetry.

best_practices: Run only on systems where investigation and telemetry collection are authorized.
Test queries in a representative lab and verify table schemas before production deployment.
Encrypt results, restrict access, define retention, and preserve timestamps for chain of custody.
anti_patterns: Do not collect password, token, private-key, or registry secret contents when metadata is sufficient.
Do not deploy broad scheduled queries without platform filters, baselines, and resource measurements.
Do not execute privileged installation or service commands without explicit approval and package integrity verification.

faq.question: Does this skill install osquery automatically?
faq.answer: No. It includes deployment guidance, but installation and service changes require explicit authorization and elevated access.

faq.question: Which operating systems are covered?
faq.answer: The material covers Linux, macOS, and Windows, although table availability varies by osquery version and platform.

faq.question: Are the bundled queries read-only?
faq.answer: The osquery examples are read-only, but their results can contain sensitive system, user, process, network, and file metadata.

faq.question: Can it replace a full forensic suite?
faq.answer: No. It supports live endpoint interrogation but does not provide disk imaging, memory acquisition, deleted-file recovery, or independent evidence validation.

faq.question: Can the query packs run without testing?
faq.answer: No. Validate schemas, performance, event-table prerequisites, expected volume, and false positives in a representative lab first.

faq.question: How should investigation results be protected?
faq.answer: Use encrypted storage, strict access controls, limited retention, audit logging, and documented handling procedures appropriate for forensic evidence.
